elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted 21.4 says only "Each other Party shall indemnify Teleglobe USA Inc." — there is no "defend" (or "hold harmless") verb and no reference to Customer's affiliates. To reach preferred, add an express defence obligation extending to Teleglobe USA Inc. and its affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 21.4 runs in favour of "Teleglobe USA Inc." alone; affiliates are not named, and retained 21.2 is mutual rather than Customer-protective. Add "and its affiliates" to the indemnified parties.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: 21.4: indemnity "against any claim by a third party that the APCN 2, or any equipment, facility or software supplied by that Party, infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right" — the supply-side analogue of Services/Deliverables in this consortium agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The inserted trigger is limited to IP infringement/misappropriation; no breach-of-law limb appears in 21.4, 21.2 or Paragraph 32. Add a limb for the indemnifying Party's breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No unauthorised access/disclosure of Customer Data limb anywhere in the rendered language; 21.4 covers IP claims only.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: 21.4 contains no gross negligence or wilful misconduct trigger; retained 21.2 is a proportional third-party ownership-claim share only.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic in 21.4; Paragraph 32 addresses reimbursement after judgment/approved settlement, not claim notice by the indemnified Party. Add a prompt-notice provision.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: 21.4 is silent on defence control; retained 21.2 gives the indemnifying Party only a right to "observe but not directly participate", and settlements sit with the Management Committee under 32.1. Add an express control-of-defence allocation.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation appears in 21.4 or the retained provisions.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Retained 21.2 obliges each Party (including Teleglobe USA Inc.) to indemnify the others for all third-party claims arising out of APCN 2 up to its Schedule B share — far broader than Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law; the redline deliberately left 21.2 untouched.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted 21.4 first sentence: "Each other Party shall indemnify Teleglobe USA Inc. against any claim by a third party that the APCN 2, or any equipment, facility or software supplied by that Party, infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right" — one-way in our favour, correct party direction.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: 21.4: "except to the extent the infringement arises from a modification made by Teleglobe USA Inc." — permitted carve-out, correctly limited to our own modifications.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: 21.4: "from a combination with items not supplied by that Party".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: 21.4: "or from specifications furnished by Teleglobe USA Inc.".

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: 21.4: "The indemnifying Party shall procure the right for Teleglobe USA Inc. to continue using the infringing item, or modify or replace it so that it is non-infringing" — mandatory ("shall"), all three remedies present.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: 21.4: "if none of those remedies is reasonably available, shall refund the amounts paid by Teleglobe USA Inc. in respect of that item" — refund is conditioned on unavailability of the three remedies and is scoped to the item, so it captures the applicable fees.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: 21.4 final sentence: "Each indemnifying Party's aggregate liability under this Subparagraph shall not exceed three (3) times the annual O&M Costs payable by Teleglobe USA Inc." — 3× multiplier, base is the recurring annual charge we pay; confirm "O&M Costs" is a capitalised defined term in this Agreement (the supplied definitions set is empty) and conform the capitalisation if it is not.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Duplicate of the fallback IP limb; satisfied by 21.4 as quoted above.

reasons: Finding classification is correct: the Agreement's only indemnity architecture (mutual, ownership-claim, Schedule B-share indemnity in 21.2 plus the Paragraph 32 reimbursement/claims-conduct regime) contains no intellectual-property infringement trigger, no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and no super-cap, which is the walk-away case of no supplier IP indemnity and therefore a material fallback failure.

All seven fallback elements are met in operative language by the single inserted Subparagraph 21.4: one-way IP/misappropriation indemnity in our favour, the three permitted Customer-side exclusions (modification, combination, specification), mandatory procure/modify/replace remedies, a conditional refund backstop scoped to the affected item, and an express 3× annual O&M Costs cap. Position-complete at the fallback.

Preferred level is not reached: no defence obligation, no affiliates, no breach-of-law, data-breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs, no notice/control/cooperation procedure, and Customer's own indemnity under 21.2 remains broad rather than limited to Customer-provided content and breach of law. That is consistent with the stated fallback-only strategy but must not be described as the preferred position.

Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, the favourable mutual 21.2 and Paragraph 32 mechanics are retained verbatim, and the insertion carries no extras beyond the checklist (no attorneys' fees limb, survival tail, at-own-expense language, claims procedure or added damages categories). The 3× multiplier sits exactly at, not above, the fallback threshold.

Intent is preserved — 21.4 operates as a free-standing additional obligation and does not contradict 21.2's Schedule B proviso (which is scoped to that subparagraph) or 32.1's reimbursement proportions. Two drafting hygiene points to tidy: (i) consider opening 21.4 with "Without prejudice to Subparagraph 21.2 and Paragraph 32" so the new full-value IP indemnity is plainly cumulative rather than absorbed into the proportional-share mechanics; and (ii) confirm the numbering slot 21.4 is free and that "O&M Costs" matches the Agreement's defined term.
